title: Grounded Reasoning Systems for Cloud Architecture - Iman Makaremi
talk_summary: A cloud-architecture copilot team describes grounding agents in structured context (semantic enrichment, graph retrieval, requirement templates) and orchestrating a chief-architect + staff-architect + retriever multi-agent system with isolated memory, agent cloning for parallelism, and human eval tooling. Most claims are qualitative; the transferable mechanisms are memory isolation, cloning for fan-out, structured outputs, and human-in-the-loop eval.

takeaways.technique: Isolate memory per agent instead of sharing one growing context
takeaways.what_they_do: Each agent keeps its own conversation memory rather than a shared pool, both to save tokens and because they observed more memory increased hallucination.
takeaways.evidence_quote: increasing the memory showed increase of hostination in the in the results. So we decided to keep the memory isolated

takeaways.technique: Clone an agent per work item for parallel fan-out with inherited history
takeaways.what_they_do: After conflict resolution, each staff architect is cloned once per recommendation to produce proposals in parallel; each clone inherits prior history then diverges with its own.
takeaways.evidence_quote: each staff architect is going to be cloned uh by the number of recommendations that's supposed to generate and each clone has access to the past history

takeaways.technique: Explicit control flow with a manager over sub-workflows
takeaways.what_they_do: They insist multi-agent systems need defined control flow and a manager layer on top of per-task workflows rather than letting agents free-run.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's not possible to have multiple agents to just work with each other and uh uh hope for the best

takeaways.technique: Structured outputs / templates for inter-agent messages
takeaways.what_they_do: They moved from free-form/XML parsing to structured message formats and requirement templates so downstream agents get predictable fields.
takeaways.evidence_quote: structured outputs improves clarity and control. It's super super important to to do structured outputs

takeaways.technique: Human eval tool with per-case trace inspection, baked in from design
takeaways.what_they_do: They built an internal tool ('eagle eye') to inspect each case's inputs, agent conversations, and outputs, score relevance/clarity, and drive next priorities; they found LLM evals insufficient and confidence ≠ correctness.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the best uh evaluation is human evaluation. Uh and we noticed that LLM evaluations uh are good but they do not give us what we want

takeaways.technique: Graph-based retrieval over structured entities instead of pure vector search
takeaways.what_they_do: They found semantic/vector search weak on graph-shaped data and moved to graph-enhanced component search plus semantic enrichment of nodes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: semantic search doesn't work very well for uh uh this type of graph data and it has its own limitation
